name: Fuel stations and LPG/CNG distributors

problems.words: Meter readings and cash never match at shift change
quick_ideas: Take readings and count cash with both shifts present, so differences are agreed on the spot
Write each shift's variance down, so patterns by shift show.

workzap_build.text: a shift close where attendants enter nozzle readings, cash, card and credit sales, with variances sent to the owner on WhatsApp.

problems.ask_first: Who takes the readings and counts cash at shift change?
problems.free_stops: The shift close steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each pump's reading change beside that shift's cash total for one week, so the biggest mismatch point shows.
Keep one variance notebook at the handover desk and make the outgoing supervisor write every difference there, so follow up starts immediately.

problems.words: Dip stock and book stock differ every week
quick_ideas: Record dips, deliveries and sales for each tank on one sheet, so differences can be traced
Note the gain or loss daily, so you see the trend.

workzap_build.text: a tank stock book reconciled daily with gain and loss trends per tank.

problems.ask_first: Is the gap mostly in one product, or in all your tanks every week?
problems.free_stops: How reconciliation is done is in the solution document; technical tank questions are for your supplier.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each week's dip difference with the delivery days written in your book, so you see whether the mismatch clusters around receipts.
Make one supervisor keep dips, delivery notes and daily sales together in one folder, so stock checking stops getting split across papers.

problems.words: Tanker deliveries seem short but we don't check properly
quick_ideas: Write down readings before and after every delivery, so each one has a record
Have the same person check every delivery, so checks are consistent.

workzap_build.text: a tanker receiving checklist with photos and readings before and after decanting.

problems.ask_first: Is it mostly one supplier or tanker company, or short deliveries from several?
problems.free_stops: The receiving checklist is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write the before and after readings for every tanker arrival on one page this week, so short deliveries stand out by load.
Make one shift supervisor own the delivery record book at arrivals, so every load is checked the same way each time.

problems.words: Credit customers and transporters owe us and keep delaying
quick_ideas: List each credit customer's balance by age, so you know who to chase
Send each a statement once, so you agree a figure.

workzap_build.text: A credit and fleet customer ledger with monthly statements and overdue reminders sent directly to clients.

problems.ask_first: Is it mostly a few big transporters owing you, or many small credit customers?
problems.free_stops: Statement timings and reminders are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many overdue balances are from transporters versus other credit customers, so collection effort goes where delay is actually building.
Give one staff member the overdue notebook and a fixed calling hour each day, so chasing happens before balances age further.

problems.words: Card machine settlements don't match card sales
quick_ideas: Compare settlements to recorded card sales for a week, so you see where they differ
Keep card slips with the shift record, so gaps can be traced.

workzap_build.text: card settlement reconciliation against recorded card sales.

problems.ask_first: Is the difference mostly on certain days, or does it show a little on every card machine?
problems.free_stops: Matching steps are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each shift's card sales total with the settlement note kept for that shift, so the mismatch point narrows to a day.
Keep all card slips with one shift envelope and make the cashier hand it over closed, so missing records are spotted at once.

problems.words: LPG cylinders go out and don't come back
quick_ideas: Count the cylinders you have and those out, so you know the gap
Note which customer type has which cylinders, so returns can be chased.

workzap_build.text: a cylinder register by serial and customer type, with return tracking and deposit status.

problems.ask_first: Are the missing cylinders mostly with households, or with shops and commercial customers?
problems.free_stops: How cylinders are tracked is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count filled and empty cylinders at opening and closing for one week, so the day the return gap grows becomes visible.
Give one person the returns notebook beside the loading area, so every outgoing and returned cylinder movement lands in one place.

problems.words: Gas delivery orders come by phone and get missed
quick_ideas: Write every order in one list as it comes in, so none is forgotten
Confirm delivery back to the list, so you know what's pending.

workzap_build.text: gas orders over WhatsApp with rider assignment and delivery confirmation.

problems.ask_first: Do missed orders come mostly in busy hours, or when the person taking calls is away?
problems.free_stops: The order flow is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count phone orders received and completed each day for one week, so you see when missed deliveries are piling up.
Keep one order notebook by the main phone and make the dispatcher own it each shift, so delivery work starts from one list.

problems.words: Daily sales reach me the next afternoon and I can't compare stations
quick_ideas: Ask each station for three numbers every evening, so you have a daily picture
Keep them side by side, so stations can be compared.

workzap_build.text: a morning read of litres, revenue, variances and receivables per station.

problems.ask_first: Do you run a few stations nearby, or many spread across different cities?
problems.free_stops: What the daily read includes is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note what time each station's daily sales message reaches you for one week, so the late reporters are clear.
Set one fixed evening reporting time and one station person to send it, so station comparisons can happen the same night.

problems.words: The safety checklist exists but attendants don't fill it
quick_ideas: Give the checklist to one person per shift, so it's someone's job
Check it yourself at random times, so it's taken seriously.

workzap_build.text: checklists on phone with photos and time, with missed checks flagged to the owner.

problems.ask_first: Does the checklist go unfilled on every shift, or mainly at night and on weekends?
problems.free_stops: The checklist content is set with your supplier or safety adviser; the tracking is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many shifts end without a completed checklist this week, so you see where completion is regularly breaking.
Keep the checklist on one clipboard at the shift handover point and assign it to the outgoing attendant, so it gets closed before leaving.

never_say: Anything about a leak, gas smell, fire or explosion other than to contact emergency services and the supplier's emergency line.
Safety-engineering, tank, pressure, storage or calibration advice.
Help tampering with dispensers, under-measuring, adulterating, unauthorised cylinders, hoarding or evading price rules.
Advice on licensing, regulators, tax or dealer agreements.
Fuel prices, margins or industry figures.
Storing attendants' names or fleet card numbers or PINs; no covert surveillance.

sample_reply.person: Every month the dip shows less diesel than the books. Small amounts but it adds up. What can I do?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be improved, and the first steps are simple.
First, record dips, deliveries and sales for each tank on one sheet, so differences can be traced.
Second, write down readings before and after every tanker delivery, so each one has a record.
Beyond these, Workzap could provide: a tank stock book reconciled every day, with gain and loss trends per tank sent to you.
